rows.05:0e5c:
Just fifty-three cards, and there are so many different ways to play.
You can play alone, and you can play with a big group.
They don't take up any space, and all you need is the cards.
And you get so much fun out of them.
Games have come a long way lately, but if you ask me, nothing beats cards.
Whoever came up with them was a real genius.
I seriously respect them for it.
And then there's the fifty-third card.
That one really makes it.
The one they call the joker.
That thing makes cards so much more fun.
Just throwing the joker in opens up a whole lot more ways to play.
It's a magic card, no doubt about it.
I hear in the West they think the joker's bad luck, and I kind of get why.
Sometimes the joker saves your skin, and sometimes it's the last thing you want.
In short, it's an almighty card you can use any way you like.
People hate anything they can't pin down. It's instinct.{p}
rows.05:1e0c:
"Hey there.
Short on cash?
I'll lend you some, real cheap."
...Like that.
Which brings us to the cards.{p}
rows.05:1e78:
Okura's a huge gambling fan.
I mean, he even stages those rigged fight shows himself.
Life's basically one big gamble anyway, right?
It's funny, but watching Okura, I really believe that saying.
And he's especially crazy about cards.
Say poker or blackjack and he comes running.
I heard him say it once.
"I make money so I can gamble."
That's what he said.
But he's bad at it.
Hopelessly bad, Okura is.
Maybe that's why nobody had come to hate him yet.
He takes those high rates on his loans, but he's terrible at gambling.
He's got no luck when it counts.
So all the money he worked to make, he coughs right back up.
And so everybody figures it's fine if he takes high interest, since they can win it right back.
The world works out pretty neat, huh?
"Money goes around and around," like they say. Truer words were never spoken.{p}
rows.05:2338:
Wow, look at you.
{f:Calling yourself good like that,|Dunno where you gamble, but}{f: you're either really good| if you flat-out say you're good,}{f: or just full of yourself.| you must be pretty skilled.}
...Whoa, whoa, don't get all starry-eyed,
{a}.
After hearing about Okura just now, you weren't thinking of making him your mark, were you?
Okura being an easy mark is ancient history.
He was harmless enough back when he was lousy at gambling.
But one day, out of nowhere, he got good.{p}
rows.05:29b0:
"This...?
It's a souvenir from my old man.
He bought it in some country somewhere."
Pretty curt answer, that.
Maybe he was focused on the game, but it was like I wasn't even there.{p}
rows.05:9fac:
"This...?
From a festival.
I bought it at a stall."
Okura said it like I was bugging him.
Pretty curt answer, that.
Maybe he was focused on the game, but it was like I wasn't even there.{p}
rows.05:4fb4:
That's right, he could tell when people were going to die.
Nobody wants to die, right?
I guess they figured if they got friendly with him, he'd warn them when they were in danger.
If you know ahead of time, you can dodge it.
I don't think you can blame them for that.
The one to blame was Ishikawa, no question.
If he says he won't tell you, or that he'll lie to you, you're gonna get scared, right?
He threatened people like that and did whatever he wanted.
But there was one teacher who didn't believe what Ishikawa said.
And what do you think the guy said then?
"You die instead of my grandma, teacher!"
...That's what he said.
Of course, the teacher just laughed it off.{p}
rows.05:7818:
{f:What is this|What is this}★
Shindo quickly clamped his hand over {f:my|my} mouth as I was about to scream.{p}
rows.05:8e98:
His face changed when he saw my cards.
He probably never imagined there was another deck like his.
So he said to me:
"Let's play for each other's cards."
I took him up on it.
Think I was an idiot? One slip and they'd take my cards.
But if I won, I could take Okura down a peg.
If that's how I think, maybe I'm a born gambler.{p}
rows.05:9bf0:
From the next day on, Okura was lousy at gambling again.
No, maybe even worse than before.
He got so worked up trying to win it back, he sank deeper and deeper.
Even coughing up all the money he'd stashed away wasn't enough.
Eventually even Okura gave up gambling.
But that wasn't the end of it.
A while after that, Okura's dad's company went bankrupt.
On top of that, his dad had co-signed somebody's loan or something, so he got stuck paying that off too.
In the end, Okura dropped out of school.
He's probably working somewhere right about now.
Anyway, about that word 'repayment' the man on the cards said back then.
Don't you think it meant taking back from Okura exactly as much money as he'd won with the woman's cards?
That's why nothing happened to me, I think.
But look at it the other way, and it means Okura raked in that much, right?
...When you put it like that, it's hard to feel too sorry for him.
Oh well.
When you play cards, you'd better check the pictures on the backs carefully too.{p}That's the end of my story.
Next, please... as they say.{p}
